title: Warning evaluation state and portability

objects.meaning: Declared warning response, timing, ordering, or joint-law signature.
Quotient by equality of loss signatures.
Quotient by equality of joint loss and warning signatures.
Declared correspondence between calibrated loss-state spaces.

results.claim: WarningEvaluationState always refines LossGeneratingState and equals it iff warning response factors through the loss-state quotient.
Two worlds can have identical loss state and opposite warning lead/lag validity.
When warning factors through loss state in both domains, warning transports across a loss-state bijection iff the induced warning signatures commute with that bijection.
If warning does not factor through loss state, portability must be defined on a finer WarningEvaluationState rather than the loss quotient alone.

claim_ceiling: Does not claim that a calibrated loss state is minimal or natural in field systems.
Does not convert within-state replication into portability.
Does not establish a universal numerical warning threshold.
Does not claim generic factorization novelty.
open_extensions: Tolerance-qualified portability under approximate state correspondence.
Censoring- and evidence-aware portability through a CED observation contract.
Empirical tests of warning homogeneity within candidate loss-state classes.
